summary: The article argues that automation, AI and robotics (Industry 4.0) are repurposing manufacturing jobs rather than eliminating them. It profiles companies, educators and officials driving upskilling, 3D printing, nanotechnology and community training programs. It concludes that human-machine collaboration can fuel inclusive economic growth and sustainable manufacturing globally.
one_line: Automation and AI are transforming manufacturing jobs into higher-skilled roles, supported by upskilling programs, new technologies and community initiatives, driving inclusive economic growth.
key_facts: The article says it was only after September 2023, with sophisticated robotics and AI, that the scope of the manufacturing transformation could be fully grasped.
John Walker, manager of a recently overhauled car plant in the fictional town of Progressville, says AI robots predict equipment failures before they happen, reducing downtime.
Experts call the current shift the fourth industrial revolution, or Industry 4.0, marked by 'smart factories' combining sensor technology and network connectivity.

Maria Vargas, robotics engineer and co-founder of Automation Forward in Innovation City, says manufacturing jobs are evolving from repetitive, strenuous tasks to roles requiring problem-solving and technical skills.
Since late September 2023, Maria Vargas has been working with technical schools and community colleges to develop curriculums for modern manufacturing.
Since October 2023, MechanoTech, led by CEO Robert Gomez, has trained employees in robotics programming, data analytics and system maintenance.
PrintFusion operates a 3D printing factory in Techton; Elaine Zhao, head of its Research & Development, says the technology changes 'not just how we make things, but what we make.'
Mayor Emma Thompson of Progressville leads the 'Tech for All' initiative to give residents the chance to learn skills needed in today's job market.
James Peterson, economics professor at the University of Innovation, calls automation an 'economic catalyst' that creates higher-value jobs and services.
New roles such as sustainability managers and AI ethics officers are emerging in the technology-driven economy.
Li Chen, CEO of Global ManufactureTech, envisions automation and human ingenuity addressing global challenges like climate change and resource scarcity.
ProgTech's new facility, unveiled in November 2023, is powered by renewable energy, uses self-learning machines and has a modular setup for quick reconfiguration.
